Casting our eyes forward into the future it seems to me that we are going to be be more and more so faced with the question of "what's the point?". We will be faced with this dilemma as less and less of the natural dilemmas will exist. Humans won't be worried about their shelter, food, water, safety etc. Ergo once we have finished all of the things that we need to do to survive and thrive, what is left? Seemingly what's left is the question "what's the point?, why am I even here in the first point". In other words the old conundrum of "what is the meaning of life?" just worded differently.

So here goes a 24 year old musing on the answer to such a good question. To cut to the chase I think that the answer is what I will call _**C**ontinuous **I**erative **S**elf **I**mprovement_ (CISI), pronounced "sissy" for the curious^[I love coming up with new names and disregarding that someone else has probably already thought of this and written 15+ books about it. Nevermind all that **I** have given it a new name!]. Its a very simple idea and a very simple guiding belief—the bests ideas usually are simple I've been told. Its not only simple it also seem to be quite intuitive. Take these three points.

1. We are designed and built to work and do things
2. Life is supposed to do things
3. Doing things that have a purpose is better than doing things for no reason.

Then it seems CISI is a good productive and beneficial goal. There needn't be a philosophical argument that it is your moral duty or the *correct* thing to do (I believe that argument exists and is probably valid I am just not making it), all I am saying is that this goal will maximise your happiness and satisfaction in life. 

To always improve things is striving for perfection. We can acknowledge taht perfection is impossible yet the strive to meet it or make it as close as possible is a noble and worthy goal. Of course worrying about perfectionism is a concern as that can be very counter productive. Yet we can also acknowledge that some things are better than others even if the waters are a bit muddy [^1]. Furthermore I will make an unfounded assertion that for most things in your life you can roughly rank them in terms of this thing is better than the other and deep down you know what it is. In other words you know areas in your personal life or in what you do daily that you can improve on (being politer to your colleagues, appreciating the little things...).

[^1]: If you ignore that some things are better than others by saying things like "everyone is imperfect" then you are committing the [fallacy of gray](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/dLJv2CoRCgeC2mPgj/the-fallacy-of-gray), which is generally the process of replacing a binary world (this is good, this is bad) with a world in which everyone is the same (uncertain).

## It actually applies to many things.

Now what I mean by continuous interactive self improvement. I will go through each word one by one to make things clear.

Continuous means you aren't making distinguishable steps just nonstop movement in the right direction. You don't only improve on Sunday's and stayed the same the rest of the week. It also isn't something that stops based on the assumption that things will never be perfect ^[Now I know here there is a point to be made about how this sounds alot like never being content. That is partly true, but we have to look one layer deeper to see the distinction. One is never content with the status quo—not even the Dalai Lama himself. The key is that what you are trying to improve it needn't be money, power etc it can simply be contentness itself! Furthermore you can be very content with who you are and your journey will striving to improve and be better. Jesus might be considered an enlightened guy and he wasn't content with just healing one person, he wanted to improve on that and heal the world!].

Iterative is a simple one that means that you build on what was before you. What is already there is a foundation for what you are trying to do. The steps are small and incremental, but they do exist. You aren't going to go away on a retreat for 3 months and come back 'the new you who is perfect'. It is a lifestyle choice a mindset and something that you are always.

When I say self it doesn't limit this to individuals and people alone. It is instead a self referential idea that applies to everything. I would hope that civilisation itself will work to improve itself as well as my own foot muscles ability to help me balance.

Lastly is improvement. A tough one to measure and define. Rather that provide an exact definition (that is left as an exercise for the reader). Instead I will scope out how to define it. The idea of improvement requires both a destination and a measure of how far along you are. For the destination we generally want to use the idea of perfect yet the dimension that can be used is very vast. I.e. you can improve your health, your wealth, your compassion etc. Importantly not all of these dimensions are equal and we can spend time working to improve which one is most important (which is itself some that requiring sissy on, I love recursion). I would posit though that focusing inwards is where most of us need to put our attention, namely improving the operation of our own mind and our impact on the world.


## Lots of people are actually talking about CISI

To give some outside influence I can go through what I think other people talk about which seems about the same thing as CISI. A rough list based on where I am thinking right now.

| name | their idea |
|------|----------- |

| Rationality movement | As put forth by Eliezer Yudkowsky and others (i.e [less wrong](https://www.lesswrong.com/about)), its about improving your rationality and decision making skills. Always wanting to find more biases and fallacy so that one can dispell or mitigate them. |
| [Star trek: First contact](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8rh3xPatEto) | In the future they have no money as it is no longer a driving force and instead "work to better ourselves and the rest of humanity."
| [Mens groups](https://www.mensgroup.nz/about/#) | Mens groups are about men coming togather to find out better ways of being men
| [Growth Mindset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindset#Fixed_and_growth_mindsets) & [Lifelong learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifelong_learning) | The idea that you can always improve and learn new things. |
| [Aaron Schwartz](https://aaronsw.vercel.app/weblog/rawnerve) | 
| [The big leap](https://openlibrary.org/books/OL24254201M/The_Big_Leap) | The idea that we have four zones in our life (zone of incompetence, zone of competence, zone of excellence and zone of genius) and that we should always strive to be in the zone of genius. You end up with a feeling of emptiness and dissatisfaction if you don't continuously challenge yourself. |


## Where other people are wrong
A problem is that youcan end up trying to self imrpove in some aspects ofl ife and ignore others. That is no good at all either.

## How to do it

Broadly speaking I don't know. If I did know I would be avery happy and content person—which I don't feel like I am yet. The idea though is you have to both accept that you are not perfect, open your eyes to the world and then heed the call to action to improve^[This idea is the central thesis of the big leap.].
